head: claude/sweep-ch07-sec3a-printed-972a
title: Prove Printed.sLocalPrimaryPoleMultiplicity_eq_sum_orders_false (Definition 7.3.1.4, p. 343)
body:
Closes #5342

Proves `Printed.sLocalPrimaryPoleMultiplicity_eq_sum_orders_false` (Definition 7.3.1.4, (7.3.1.6)–(7.3.1.7), p. 343) in `RiemannMasullo/Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta/Sec3a_Printed.lean`.

**Counterexample.** F = ℚ, S = {(2)}, p = (2), c = 1 (the trivial quasi-character). The primary multiplicity is `card S₍₂₎ = 1` (`sLocalPrimaryPoleMultiplicity_one`). At the trivial character every selected finite place is a pole place (`sLocalPolePlaces_one`), and a finite Euler factor has a pole exactly where the restricted Tate factor has one (private `sLocalRhoPoleOrder_eq_card_polePlaces_finite` of Ch07 Sec2, reached with `import all`). So each summand on the right has negative order, the sum is ≤ 0, and it cannot equal 1. (The argument only uses the sign of the orders, not their exact value −1.)

The hypotheses are checked directly: over ℚ, `w.under (𝓞 ℚ) = w`, which gives saturation and identifies the primary part; the S-integers of ℚ have trivial Picard group because they are a localization of the PID `𝓞 ℚ` (Mathlib's `isLocalizationSInteger`), hence a UFD, hence a GCD domain.

New private helpers, directly above the theorem: `..._order_neg`, `..._under`, `..._pic`. New imports: `import all RiemannMasullo.Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta.Sec2` and `Mathlib.GroupTheory.MonoidLocalization.UniqueFactorization`. `open Classical in` added before the theorem, as on the printed definition.

**Checks run**
- `lake build RiemannMasullo.Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta.Sec3a_Printed`: ok, about 4 s for the module after a touch
- `lake build` (full): `Build completed successfully (18994 jobs)`
- `scripts/lint.sh`: `lint: ok`
- `lake env lean --run scripts/Signatures.lean RiemannMasullo.Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta.Sec3a_Printed`, before and after, then `scripts/signatures.sh --compare`: no changed declarations
- `#print axioms RiemannMasullo.Printed.sLocalPrimaryPoleMultiplicity_eq_sum_orders_false`: `[propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The `sorryAx` comes from `finiteLocalTateFactor` (Ch03 Sec3), which appears in the printed statement itself and whose existence proof upstream is still open; `#print axioms RiemannMasullo.finiteLocalTateFactor` shows the same list, while `sLocalPolePlaces_one` and `sLocalPrimaryPoleMultiplicity_one` are clean.
